fieldMarks: Long sloping 'ski-jump' profile of head and bill.
Drake: chestnut head, black bill, black chest and whitish back.
Hen: pale tan head and neck contrasting with a dark bill and grayish body.
behavior: Dives in shallow water for leaves, roots and seeds of aquatic plants (pondweeds, wild celery), plus mollusks and insects.
Drakes grunt or croak; hens quack.
Migrates late in fall and early in spring, often in V formations.
habitat: Breeds on shallow freshwater prairie marshes; winters on protected bays, estuaries, coastal salt bays and interior lakes.
range: Breeds from Alaska and western Canada through the northern Great Plains; winters on the Great Lakes, Pacific coast and mid-Atlantic coast.
